purpose: Ultra-global research registry for high-fidelity archival document image restoration, super-resolution, dewarping, denoising, binarization, OCR-aware enhancement and evidence-based visual quality assessment.

qualityTarget.engineeringMeaning: Very-high-resolution delivery only where source resolution and restoration evidence justify it; output pixel count never proves recovered historical detail.
qualityTarget.fidelityPriority: text, glyphs, diacritics, page geometry and documentary evidence over perceptual prettiness
neverClaim: 24K output means 24K source detail was recovered
a visually pleasing restoration is necessarily faithful

newCandidates.name: SwinIR
newCandidates.notes: Classical and real-world SR plus denoising and JPEG artifact reduction; x2/x3/x4/x8 research options.

newCandidates.name: HAT
newCandidates.notes: High-performing transformer SR family; benchmark fidelity versus perceptual sharpening and memory cost.

newCandidates.name: NAFNet
newCandidates.notes: Efficient conservative restoration baseline before OCR.

newCandidates.name: Restormer
newCandidates.notes: High-resolution deblurring and denoising candidate.

newCandidates.name: DiffBIR
newCandidates.notes: Diffusion blind restoration and 8x SR; strict anti-hallucination gate required.

newCandidates.name: SeeSR
newCandidates.notes: Real-world SR candidate; text fidelity must outrank perceptual quality.

newCandidates.name: HYPIR
newCandidates.notes: Research candidate only until unrestricted licensing is cleared.

newCandidates.name: SUPIR
newCandidates.notes: Research candidate only until unrestricted licensing is cleared.

newCandidates.name: TPGSR
newCandidates.notes: Text-prior guided SR; benchmark Arabic glyph and diacritic fidelity.

newCandidates.name: TATT
newCandidates.notes: Text-attention SR with deformation robustness; benchmark on Arabic script.

newCandidates.name: PEAN
newCandidates.notes: Prior-enhanced attention SR; use conservative glyph checks.

newCandidates.name: STISR-TCDM / DiMSS
newCandidates.notes: Text-conditioned diffusion SR; hallucinated-glyph gate mandatory.

newCandidates.name: RTSRN
newCandidates.notes: Robust text SR candidate for benchmark comparison.

newCandidates.name: DocRes
newCandidates.notes: Unified document dewarping, deshadowing, appearance restoration, deblurring and binarization.

newCandidates.name: DocNLC
newCandidates.notes: Multi-degradation document enhancement.

newCandidates.name: UVDoc
newCandidates.notes: Neural document unwarping with benchmarked alternatives.

newCandidates.name: DocScanner
newCandidates.notes: Robust document rectification with OCR-oriented evaluation.

newCandidates.name: DewarpNet
newCandidates.notes: 3D+2D document unwarping baseline.

newCandidates.name: DocTr++
newCandidates.notes: Distorted-document rectification candidate.

newCandidates.name: LA-DocFlatten
newCandidates.notes: Layout-aware flattening; dataset terms are independently gated.

newCandidates.name: Marior
newCandidates.notes: Margin removal and iterative rectification reference.

newCandidates.name: DocDiff
newCandidates.notes: Residual diffusion document enhancement; evaluate text fidelity and historical marks.

newCandidates.name: ScanTailor Advanced
newCandidates.notes: Deterministic scanned-book cleanup, binarization and background/foreground separation.

newCandidates.name: unpaper
newCandidates.notes: Deterministic scanned-page cleanup for OCR preprocessing.

newCandidates.name: OCRmyPDF image-processing
newCandidates.notes: Rotate, deskew, background cleanup and oversampling; visual review required.

newCandidates.name: DocDiff
newCandidates.notes: Document-specific diffusion restoration; same-source text fidelity gate applies.

newCandidates.name: TAIR
newCandidates.notes: ICLR 2026 text-aware restoration with SA-Text and Real-Text evaluation; strong research candidate for text-first restoration.

newCandidates.name: TiGeSR
newCandidates.notes: CVPR 2026 two-stage text-first restoration: glyph restoration then image enhancement. Third-party base model and dataset terms remain separate.

newCandidates.name: TADiSR
newCandidates.notes: 4x diffusion SR with text masks; base-model terms must be audited separately.

newCandidates.name: DocIQ / DIQA-5000
newCandidates.notes: 5,000 enhanced document images with human quality ratings for overall quality, sharpness and color fidelity.

newCandidates.name: DeQA-Doc
newCandidates.notes: VQualA 2025 DIQA champion; quality scoring can be used before expensive restoration stages.

newCandidates.name: PreP-OCR
newCandidates.notes: Two-stage historical document restoration plus OCR post-correction; useful for restoration-to-recognition coupling.

newCandidates.name: NautilusOCR
newCandidates.notes: METS/ALTO-based production OCR enhancement pipeline with quality prediction; strong cultural-heritage workflow reference.

newCandidates.name: NDNP-Open-OCR
newCandidates.notes: Library of Congress pipeline for large-scale historical OCR reprocessing into ALTO/PDF.

newCandidates.name: pero-enhance
newCandidates.notes: Integrated enhancement and OCR workflow with editable OCR XML feedback loop.

newCandidates.name: pero-quality
newCandidates.notes: Page-level quality heatmaps and OCR-confidence-derived readability estimates.

newCandidates.name: AutoHDR
newCandidates.notes: Historical document repair research candidate; non-commercial research restriction means it cannot enter unrestricted production without permission.

newCandidates.name: DiffHDR / HDR28K
newCandidates.notes: Historical Document Repair dataset with 28,552 damaged/repaired pairs and character-level annotations; valuable for damage-aware benchmarks.

newCandidates.name: A-FINE / DiffIQA
newCandidates.notes: Large human-annotated relative-quality dataset; useful as auxiliary evidence, not as a document-specific authority.

newCandidates.name: TextDiff
newCandidates.notes: Mask-guided residual diffusion for scene-text SR; include only as research comparison.

newCandidates.name: RGDiffSR
newCandidates.notes: Recognition-guided diffusion SR; strong conceptual comparator for OCR-aware restoration.

24kPolicy.preferredDelivery: 24K-class derivative only when justified; otherwise retain highest faithful native restoration resolution

promotionRules: No generative restoration may replace the immutable original.
A candidate that improves visual quality but increases OCR-CER, glyph errors or hallucinated-glyph-rate is rejected for archival text restoration.
24K-class output is a delivery target, never proof of recovered historical detail.
Text-preservation benchmarks outrank generic photographic perceptual scores for books.
Every model weight, base model and training dataset must pass a separate rights gate.
Neural and deterministic pipelines must be compared on identical source pages.
The selected pipeline may be an ensemble or staged cascade rather than a single engine.
Document quality assessment must precede expensive restoration when it can prevent harmful processing.
Human approval is mandatory before an enhanced page becomes a faithful archival derivative.
notes: TAIR, TiGeSR and TADiSR are especially valuable because they explicitly make text structure part of restoration rather than treating text as an ordinary texture.
DocIQ/DIQA-5000 and DeQA-Doc add an evidence layer for deciding whether a page should be enhanced and whether enhancement actually improved it.
AutoHDR is intentionally license-gated because its stated CC BY-NC-ND restriction is incompatible with unrestricted production redistribution.
PreP-OCR and NautilusOCR show that the strongest production design may combine image restoration, OCR confidence, post-correction and iterative human feedback rather than relying on one image model.
The study/evaluation registry is research infrastructure; it does not grant rights to any third-party book, scan, dataset or model.
